name: General-purpose control relay (SPDT/DPDT, 24 VAC coil)
function: Low-current switching: a 24 VAC coil moves NO/NC contacts to bring on fans, heat, economizer inputs, or interlocks. Common as blower, condenser fan, and heat relays.

designation.note: Exact relay designations come from the LCH wiring diagram.

location.value: Control panel, 24V section. On the diagram: coil between an M2 output and common; contacts in the circuit it controls.

lennox-lch240.sequenceRole: Lets the M2 switch loads its board outputs can't carry directly.

trane-tsc072.sequenceRole: Controller output drives the coil; contacts switch fan or heat circuits.

failureModes.name: Coil open
failureModes.goodVsBad: Coil reads OL. 24V present, contacts never change state.
failureModes.symptoms: The load it controls never comes on.

failureModes.name: Coil shorted
failureModes.goodVsBad: Coil reads far below rated range; pops the control fuse.
failureModes.symptoms: Blown 24V fuse when that output energizes.

failureModes.name: NO contacts welded
failureModes.goodVsBad: NO reads continuity with the coil de-energized.
failureModes.symptoms: Load runs constantly (e.g. blower won't shut off, heat stays on).

failureModes.name: NO contacts burned open
failureModes.goodVsBad: Coil energizes (you hear/see it), but NO stays OL.
failureModes.symptoms: Load never comes on; looks like a dead motor or a missing call.

failureModes.name: High-resistance contacts
failureModes.goodVsBad: Energized NO reads over a fraction of an ohm; under load it drops voltage and heats up.
failureModes.symptoms: Intermittent load, especially when hot. Classic 'works when I'm here' call.

test.meter: Ω with the relay out or leads lifted; VAC at the coil in circuit.
procedure: In circuit, with the call present: 24V across the coil? If not, the problem is upstream.
LOTO, verify dead, pull the relay or lift leads.
De-energized: NO should read OL, NC near 0 Ω.
Energize the coil from a 24V source: NO near 0 Ω, NC OL. Anything in between is high-resistance contacts.
safety: Some relay contacts switch line voltage (fan motors, heat). Treat contact terminals as live until verified dead.
Lift leads before ohming or you'll read through the rest of the circuit.

coilOhms.note: Typical 24 VAC relay coil range. Use the coil resistance on the relay's spec sheet.

contactOhmsMax.note: Closed contacts over 0.5 Ω = marginal; over 5 Ω = bad.

symptoms.customer: "Fan won't shut off" (welded) or "blowing warm" / "freezing up" (blower relay open).
symptoms.tech: Load and call don't agree. Call present, load off; or no call, load running.

confusedWith: Failed blower relay looks like a frozen coil call (compressor runs, no airflow, coil ices)
Burned-open condenser fan relay looks like a dead fan motor or capacitor
Welded heat relay looks like a stuck thermostat

tests.label: Contacts, energized
tests.setup: 24 VAC applied to coil from bench supply; meter on contacts only (not a live load).

labCases.explanation: Coil in range, contacts swap state cleanly with near-zero closed resistance.

labCases.context: Complaint: blower runs all night with the store closed.
labCases.explanation: NO closed with no coil power = welded. That's the blower that won't quit.

labCases.context: No heat. 24V present at the relay coil terminals, nothing clicks.
labCases.explanation: OL coil. 24V got there and had nowhere to go.

labCases.context: Intermittent: fan drops out on hot afternoons.

tests.label: Contacts, energized
tests.setup: 24 VAC to coil from bench supply.

labCases.explanation: 1.8 Ω across closed contacts is high. It works cold, then cooks under load. Replace it. That's your intermittent.
